mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters, or GDP growth recovers before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or inflation does not rise in response.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the decline in INDPRO reverses within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in RSAFS (consumer savings) signals that monetary tightening is being transmitted to household balance sheets, reducing discretionary spending and weighing on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases while RSAFS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant in a regression.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in HOUST and GDPC1 signals rising residential investment and overall economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the GDP and housing signals decouple within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above trend for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above trend for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the labor market cools before the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in CPIAUCSL above 4% while FEDFUNDS remains below 3% signals unmet inflation expectations and a delayed policy response, which erodes real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% and FEDFUNDS < 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 70% of triggered months, or the CPI spike is transitory and reverts within the week.
